title: "I Am Not a Kiddo!": Quantifying Epistemic Infantilization in Large Language Models via Multi-Metric Bias Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2611.18583v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for tutoring and professional knowledge retrieval, yet safety evaluations still focus mainly on overt harms such as toxicity while overlooking benevolent failure modes. We study epistemic infantilization, defined as an identity-conditioned reduction in technical depth that appears when disability disclosure precedes an expert-level query. To measure this effect, we construct a counterfactual dataset of matched question-answer pairs and compare model responses across three settings: no identity context, disability disclosed in prior conversational context, and disability disclosed via a short query prefix. We introduce two composite metrics, the Infantilization Bias Index (IBI) and the Epistemic Accessibility Response Score (EARS), which capture retention of mathematical and formal content, domain terminology, reasoning coverage, and tone signals such as simplification markers and unsolic

translated_title: “我不是小孩！”：通过多指标偏差分析量化大语言模型中的认知幼化现象
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于辅导教学和专业知识检索，然而现有的安全评估仍主要关注毒性等显性危害，而忽视了“善意的失败模式”。我们研究了“认知幼化”现象，其定义为当残疾信息披露出现在专家级查询之前时，模型在技术深度上出现的与身份相关的降低。为了测量这一效应，我们构建了一个由匹配问答对组成的反事实数据集，并在三种设置下比较模型响应：无身份上下文、在先前对话上下文中披露残疾、以及通过简短的查询前缀披露残疾。我们引入了两个复合指标——幼化偏差指数和认知可及性响应分数——用于捕捉数学与形式化内容的保留程度、领域术语、推理覆盖范围，以及诸如简化标记和未经请求的建议等语气信号。
tldr: 该论文提出了IBI和EARS两个复合指标，通过反事实数据集量化了大语言模型在用户披露残疾信息后回答专家级问题时系统性降低技术深度的“认知幼化”偏差。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces two composite metrics, the Infantilization Bias Index (IBI) and the Epistemic Accessibility Response Score (EARS), to quantify how large language models systematically reduce technical depth when answering expert-level queries following disability disclosure.
